```{r}
  mutate(Station = str_to_title(stn_name),
         `Change %` = round(change_pct * 100, 1),
         `Change per weekday` = round(change / weekdays_may22),
         `Upgraded interchange` = upgraded)

as_leaflet(
  network_context() +
  tm_shape(net_new_sf) + tm_lines(col = "#d95f02", lwd = 3, col_alpha = 0.8) +
  tm_shape(impact_view %>% filter(abs(change_pct) < 0.01)) +
  tm_dots(fill = "grey70", size = 0.35, id = "Station",
          popup.vars = c("Change %", "Change per weekday")) +
  tm_shape(impact_view %>% filter(abs(change_pct) >= 0.01)) +
  tm_dots(fill = "change_pct", size = 0.6,
             fill.scale = tm_scale_intervals(style = "fixed",
                                             breaks = c(-1, -0.3, -0.15, -0.05, 0, 0.05, 0.3, 2),
                                             values = "brewer.rd_bu", midpoint = 0,
                                             labels = c("< -30%", "-30 to -15%", "-15 to -5%",
                                                        "-5 to 0%", "0 to 5%", "5 to 30%", "> 30%")),
             fill.legend = tm_legend(title = "Change in AM tap-ins"),
             id = "Station",
             popup.vars = c("Change %", "Change per weekday", "Upgraded interchange")) +
  tm_shape(new_stations %>% mutate(Station = str_to_title(stn_name))) +
  tm_dots(fill = "#d95f02", size = 0.35, id = "Station"))
```

```{r}
#| label: impact-numbers
#| include: false
diverted <- sum(new_pred$pred_exp)
share_div <- diverted / sum(y_obs)
n_affected <- sum(abs(impact$change_pct) >= 0.05)
n_loss15 <- sum(impact$change_pct <= -0.15)
med_abs <- median(abs(impact$change_pct))
upg <- impact %>% filter(upgraded) %>% arrange(desc(change_pct))
west_loss <- impact %>% filter(stn_code %in% c("EW28", "EW26", "EW25", "EW29")) %>% arrange(change_pct)
```

The new stations capture about `r pct(share_div)` of all morning boardings. Under the fixed-population assumption this is diverted demand, not new demand. The impact is **local**: the median existing station changes by only `r pct(med_abs)`, `r n_affected` of 164 stations change by 5% or more, and `r n_loss15` lose 15% or more. These losses form three clusters, each next to a new line.

- **West (JRL).** The EWL stations between Jurong East and Joo Koon lose most heavily: `r str_c(str_to_title(west_loss$stn_name), " (", pct(west_loss$change_pct, 0), ")", collapse = ", ")`. Their catchments in Jurong West and Boon Lay are taken by Gek Poh, Jurong West, Bahar Junction and Tawas. The Bukit Panjang LRT and Bukit Batok stations lose residents to Choa Chu Kang West, Tengah and Bukit Batok West.
- **North-east (CRL1).** Kovan, Buangkok, Serangoon, Lorong Chuan, Bishan, Yio Chu Kang and the TEL stations at Mayflower, Upper Thomson and Lentor lose residents to Serangoon North, Tavistock and Teck Ghee.
- **East (CRL1).** Tampines, Tampines East and Upper Changi lose residents to Tampines North and Pasir Ris East.

**Interchange upgrades do not guarantee growth.** Of the seven upgraded stations, `r str_c(str_to_title(upg$stn_name[upg$change_pct > 0]), collapse = ", ")` gain riders. `r str_c(str_to_title(upg$stn_name[upg$change_pct < 0]), collapse = ", ")` *lose* morning tap-ins despite the extra line, because several new stations open inside their former catchments and the added attraction does not offset the shorter walk to the new station. These counts are tap-ins only: transfers do not tap in, so platform and corridor loads at *every* upgraded interchange will still rise as passengers change between lines. For operators, the stations losing 15% or more of their boardings are where feeder-bus routes, and possibly train frequencies, should be reviewed first.

# Market areas before and after {#sec-market}

Following Chapter 18, each subzone is assigned to the station with the highest patronage probability (its **dominant station**), and the probability surface of one affected station is mapped before and after.

```{r}
#| label: market-areas
dominant <- function(shares) shares %>%
  group_by(SUBZONE_N) %>% slice_max(p_ij, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>% ungroup() %>%
  select(SUBZONE_N, stn_code, p_ij)

dom_base <- dominant(shares_base)
dom_exp  <- dominant(shares_exp)

market_change <- origins_poly %>%
  left_join(dom_base %>% rename(dom_before = stn_code, p_before = p_ij), by = "SUBZONE_N") %>%
  left_join(dom_exp %>% rename(dom_after = stn_code, p_after = p_ij), by = "SUBZONE_N") %>%
  mutate(change = case_when(
    dom_before == dom_after ~ "Unchanged",
    dom_after %in% new_stations$stn_code ~ "Captured by a new station",
    TRUE ~ "Switched to another existing station"))

market_change %>% st_drop_geometry() %>%
  group_by(change) %>% summarise(subzones = n(), residents = fmt(sum(pop)))
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-market-switch
#| fig-cap: "Interactive map: subzones whose dominant (most-probable) boarding station changes once JRL and CRL1 open. Essentially unpopulated subzones (fewer than 100 residents, or fewer than 100 per km², such as the Murai training area) are not shaded, so that large empty areas do not dominate the map. Click a subzone to see its old and new dominant station."
station_names <- bind_rows(st_drop_geometry(stations), st_drop_geometry(new_stations)) %>%
  select(stn_code, stn_name)
market_view <- market_change %>%
  populated_for_map() %>%
  filter(change != "Unchanged") %>%
  mutate(Subzone = str_to_title(SUBZONE_N),
         `Before` = str_to_title(station_names$stn_name[match(dom_before, station_names$stn_code)]),
         `After` = str_to_title(station_names$stn_name[match(dom_after, station_names$stn_code)]),
         Residents = pop)

as_leaflet(
  tm_shape(market_view) +
  tm_polygons(fill = "change",
              fill.scale = tm_scale_categorical(values = c("Captured by a new station" = "#d95f02",
                                                           "Switched to another existing station" = "#7570b3")),
              fill.legend = tm_legend(title = "Dominant station"), fill_alpha = 0.6,
              col = "white", lwd = 1, id = "Subzone",
              popup.vars = c("Before", "After", "Residents")) +
  network_context() +
  tm_shape(net_new_sf) + tm_lines(col = "#d95f02", lwd = 3) +
  tm_shape(new_stations %>% mutate(Station = str_to_title(stn_name))) +
  tm_dots(fill = "black", size = 0.35, id = "Station"))
```

```{r}
#| include: false
mc <- market_change %>% st_drop_geometry()
n_new <- sum(mc$change == "Captured by a new station")
pop_new <- sum(mc$pop[mc$change == "Captured by a new station"])

```

Only `r n_new` of 286 populated subzones (`r fmt(pop_new)` residents) change their dominant station to a new one, and `r n_sw` more switch to a different existing station. The shifts form three groups:

- **West.** Teban Gardens and Penjuru Crescent (Jurong East) move to Pandan Reservoir. Wenya, Boon Lay Place and Yunnan (Jurong West) move to Jurong West and Gek Poh. Bukit Batok West and Brickworks move to Bukit Batok West and Tengah Park, Peng Siang to Choa Chu Kang West, and Forest Hill to Tengah. The industrial subzones of Tukang, Liu Fang and Samulun move to their JRL stations.
- **North-east.** Serangoon North, Serangoon Garden and Seletar Hills move to Serangoon North and Tavistock. Trafalgar moves to the upgraded Hougang interchange.
- **East.** Pasir Ris Drive, Flora Drive, Loyang, Tampines North and Paya Lebar North move to Pasir Ris East, Loyang and Tampines North.

Everywhere else, including the whole of the city centre, the north and the south-west, the dominant station is unchanged. The new lines reshape market areas locally rather than system-wide.


The station with the largest absolute loss is `r str_to_title(focal$stn_name)`, which loses about `r fmt(-focal$change / weekdays_may22)` morning tap-ins per weekday (`r pct(focal$change_pct, 0)`). Before the new lines it is the most likely boarding station for a broad belt of Jurong West. Afterwards, the number of subzones in which it has at least a 20% share falls from `r focal_core$sz_over_20[1]` to `r focal_core$sz_over_20[2]`. Its residential market shrinks from about `r fmt(focal_core$pop_weighted[1])` to `r fmt(focal_core$pop_weighted[2])` "expected residents" as Gek Poh, Tawas and Jurong West stations open inside its former catchment. It keeps a smaller walk-in core around the station itself.

# Value-added analysis {#sec-va}

Three additional analyses address questions the core Huff model cannot answer:

1. **Are the low-boarding JRL stations really "ghost stations"?** The Huff model only sees *home-end* demand. An alternative probabilistic spatial interaction model, the **Multiplicative Competitive Interaction (MCI) model**, is calibrated on observed station-to-station choice shares to predict *destination-end* demand at the new stations (@sec-va-mci).
2. **Are the Huff model's errors spatially structured?** (@sec-va-moran)
3. **Who gains rail access from the new lines?** (@sec-va-access)

## An alternative probabilistic SIM: MCI destination-choice model {#sec-va-mci}

**Question.** Eight new stations fall below today's lower quartile of morning *boardings* (@fig-new-stations). Most sit in the Jurong industrial estate, the NTU campus or the Changi aviation cluster, places people travel *to* in the morning rather than *from*. A home-end model cannot tell whether these stations will be busy as destinations, so the "ghost-risk" label may be wrong for some of them.

**Method.** The MCI model (Nakanishi & Cooper, 1974), the second probabilistic model in the `MCI` package, describes how passengers boarding at station *i* choose where to alight:

$$p_{ij} = \frac{\prod_k X_{kj}^{\beta_k}\; d_{ij}^{\beta_d}}{\sum_{l \ne i} \prod_k X_{kl}^{\beta_k}\; d_{il}^{\beta_d}}$$

Here $d_{ij}$ is the **rail network distance** and the $X_{kj}$ are destination attributes: job, education and residential floor area within 800 m (from the Master Plan land use), lines served, and an MRT indicator. Unlike the Huff model, which assumes its parameters, the MCI model is *estimated* from observed choice shares, here the weekday morning-peak flows between all pairs of the 164 stations. The log-centering transformation turns it into a linear regression whose coefficients are the elasticities $\beta$.

Two implementation choices need explaining:

- **A custom estimator.** `MCI::mci.transmat()` and `mci.fit()` assume every origin faces the *same* set of destinations. In station-to-station data the boarding station itself is never a destination, so each origin has a different choice set of 163 stations. The log-centering transformation is therefore applied with `dplyr` and estimated by OLS. The first chunk confirms that this reproduces `MCI::mci.fit()` exactly on a complete matrix.
- **A continuity correction.** About 15% of station pairs have zero observed flow, and log-centering cannot take logs of zero, so 0.5 trips are added to every pair. This is the standard correction for zero cells in log-linear models.

```{r}
#| label: va-mci-validate
lc_fit <- function(df, origin, vars, share) {
  lc <- df %>%
    group_by(.data[[origin]]) %>%
    mutate(across(all_of(c(share, vars)), \(x) log(x) - mean(log(x)), .names = "{.col}_lc")) %>%
    ungroup()
  lm(as.formula(str_c(share, "_lc ~ 0 + ", str_c(vars, "_lc", collapse = " + "))), data = lc)
}

# Check against MCI::mci.fit() on a complete synthetic interaction matrix
set.seed(626)
toy <- expand_grid(origin = sprintf("o%02d", 1:15), store = sprintf("s%02d", 1:8)) %>%
  mutate(dist = runif(n(), 0.5, 10), size = runif(n(), 1, 50),
         u = size^0.8 * dist^-1.5 * exp(rnorm(n(), 0, 0.2))) %>%
  group_by(origin) %>% mutate(share = u / sum(u)) %>% ungroup() %>% as.data.frame()

rbind(MCI_package = coef(mci.fit(toy, "origin", "store", "share", "dist", "size")),
      custom      = coef(lc_fit(toy, "origin", c("dist", "size"), "share")))
```

The two estimators agree to every decimal place.

```{r}
#| label: va-mci-fit
mci_vars <- c("net_km", "d_job", "d_edu", "d_res", "d_lines", "d_mrt")

make_mci <- function(dist_mat, stn_tbl) {
  expand_grid(orig = stn_tbl$stn_code, dest = stn_tbl$stn_code) %>%
    filter(orig != dest) %>%
    mutate(net_km = pmax(dist_mat[cbind(orig, dest)], 0.5)) %>%
    left_join(stn_tbl %>% transmute(dest = stn_code,
                                    d_job = job_ha + 1, d_edu = edu_ha + 1, d_res = res_ha + 1,
                                    d_lines = n_lines,
                                    d_mrt = if_else(lrt, 1, exp(1))),   # dummy coded as e^D
              by = "dest")
}

base_tbl <- destination_df %>% filter(status == "Existing")
mci_base <- make_mci(net_dist, base_tbl) %>%
  left_join(sim_data %>% select(orig, dest, trips), by = c("orig", "dest")) %>%
  mutate(trips = replace_na(trips, 0)) %>%
  group_by(orig) %>% mutate(p_ij = (trips + 0.5) / sum(trips + 0.5)) %>% ungroup()

mci_fit  <- lc_fit(mci_base, "orig", mci_vars, "p_ij")
mci_null <- lc_fit(mci_base, "orig", "net_km", "p_ij")
b_mci <- setNames(coef(mci_fit), mci_vars)

summary(mci_fit)$coefficients %>%
  as_tibble(rownames = "term") %>%
  mutate(term = c("Network distance (km)", "Job floor area 800 m", "Education floor area 800 m",
                  "Residential floor area 800 m", "Lines served", "MRT (not LRT-only)"),
         across(where(is.numeric), \(x) signif(x, 3)))

tibble(model = c("Distance only (null)", "Full MCI"),
       adj_R2_log_centered = c(summary(mci_null)$adj.r.squared, summary(mci_fit)$adj.r.squared))
```

```{r}
#| label: va-mci-predict
mci_predict <- function(df, O) {
  df %>%
    mutate(u = exp(as.numeric(as.matrix(log(df[mci_vars])) %*% b_mci))) %>%
    group_by(orig) %>% mutate(p = u / sum(u)) %>% ungroup() %>%
    left_join(O, by = "orig") %>%
    mutate(flow = p * O)
}

O_obs <- sim_data %>% group_by(orig) %>% summarise(O = sum(trips))
mci_in <- mci_predict(mci_base, O_obs)
alight_fit <- mci_in %>% group_by(stn_code = dest) %>%
  summarise(observed = sum(trips), predicted = sum(flow))

tibble(pair_R2 = cor(mci_in$trips, mci_in$flow)^2,
       alighting_R2 = cor(alight_fit$observed, alight_fit$predicted)^2)
```

**Robustness: OpenStreetMap POIs as alternative attractors.** The handout recommends OSM points of interest, so the model is re-estimated with POI counts within 800 m (food & retail, education, health, leisure & civic), first added to and then replacing the land-use attractors.

```{r}
#| label: va-mci-poi
mci_base_poi <- mci_base %>%
  left_join(base_tbl %>% transmute(dest = stn_code, d_food = poi_food_retail + 1,
                                   d_poi_edu = poi_edu + 1, d_health = poi_health + 1,
                                   d_leisure = poi_leisure_civic + 1), by = "dest")
poi_vars <- c("d_food", "d_poi_edu", "d_health", "d_leisure")
spec_mci <- list("Land use (selected)" = mci_vars,
                 "Land use + OSM POIs" = c(mci_vars, poi_vars),
                 "OSM POIs instead of land use" = c("net_km", poi_vars, "d_lines", "d_mrt"))

imap_dfr(spec_mci, \(vv, nm) {
  f <- lc_fit(mci_base_poi, "orig", vv, "p_ij")
  b <- setNames(coef(f), vv)
  pr <- mci_base_poi %>%
    mutate(u = exp(as.numeric(as.matrix(log(mci_base_poi[vv])) %*% b))) %>%
    group_by(orig) %>% mutate(p = u / sum(u)) %>% ungroup() %>%
    left_join(O_obs, by = "orig") %>% mutate(flow = p * O)
  al <- pr %>% group_by(dest) %>% summarise(obs = sum(trips), pred = sum(flow))
  tibble(specification = nm, parameters = length(vv),
         adj_R2_log_centered = summary(f)$adj.r.squared,
         alighting_R2 = cor(al$obs, al$pred)^2)
}) %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, 3)))

destination_df %>% filter(status != "Existing") %>%
  transmute(stn_name = str_to_title(stn_name), job_floor_ha = round(job_ha),
            poi_food_retail, poi_edu, poi_health) %>%
  arrange(poi_food_retail) %>% head(8)
```

The POIs add almost nothing, and the reason matters for forecasting. Adding them to the land-use model barely changes the log-centered fit, and the POI coefficients take conflicting signs because POI counts are strongly correlated with each other and with land use. Replacing land use with POIs gives a similar fit for *existing* stations. For *new* stations, however, the two sources diverge sharply: Jurong Pier, Tukang, Loyang and Aviation Park have almost no POIs today but hundreds of hectares of planned job floor space. OpenStreetMap records what **has been built**, while the Master Plan records what **is planned**. For predicting stations that open in 2028–2030 in areas still under development, the Master Plan land use is the appropriate attractor, so it is retained.

```{r}
#| label: va-mci-numbers
#| include: false
mci_ct <- summary(mci_fit)$coefficients
adj_full <- summary(mci_fit)$adj.r.squared; adj_null <- summary(mci_null)$adj.r.squared
alight_r2 <- cor(alight_fit$observed, alight_fit$predicted)^2
```

**Estimated model.** The coefficients behave as a destination model should:

- **Distance:** a 1% longer network trip lowers a destination's share by about `r round(abs(b_mci["net_km"]), 2)`%.
- **Rail service:** an MRT station draws about $e^{\beta} \approx$ `r round(exp(b_mci["d_mrt"]), 0)` times the share of an otherwise similar LRT-only halt, and each doubling of lines served multiplies the share by about `r round(2^b_mci["d_lines"], 1)`.
- **Jobs and education:** job floor space (t = `r round(mci_ct["d_job_lc", "t value"], 0)`) and education floor space (t = `r round(mci_ct["d_edu_lc", "t value"], 0)`) both raise a destination's share.
- **Residential floor space:** no effect (t = `r round(mci_ct["d_res_lc", "t value"], 1)`). This is expected, since morning trips end at workplaces and schools, not at homes, and it confirms that the model separates destination demand from the home-end demand handled by the Huff model.
- **Fit:** the attributes raise the adjusted R² of the log-centered model from `r round(adj_null, 2)` (distance only) to `r round(adj_full, 2)`, and the model reproduces total morning alightings at existing stations with R² = `r round(alight_r2, 2)`.

Most of the remaining variation comes from destinations the attributes cannot describe, such as hospitals, the airport and major schools. The fit is therefore weaker than that of the doubly constrained SIM (@sec-sim). The trade-off is deliberate: the doubly constrained SIM cannot be applied to a station that does not yet exist, whereas the MCI model can.

**Prediction for the 2030 network.** The calibrated MCI model is applied to the expanded network (193 stations, network distances recomputed on the expanded rail graph). Morning boardings at every station come from the Huff scenario, so the two models are chained: **Huff → where residents board, MCI → where those passengers alight.**

```{r}
#| label: va-mci-scenario
net_dist_exp <- distances(g_exp, weights = edges_exp$w_km)
exp_tbl <- destination_df %>% mutate(n_lines = n_lines_2030)
mci_exp <- make_mci(net_dist_exp, exp_tbl)

alight_exp <- mci_predict(mci_exp, scenario %>% transmute(orig = stn_code, O = pred_exp)) %>%
  group_by(stn_code = dest) %>% summarise(alight_pred = sum(flow))

am_alight_obs <- am_peak %>% count(stn_code = DESTINATION_PT_CODE, wt = TOTAL_TRIPS, name = "am_alight")
existing_use <- demand %>% select(stn_code, am_tapin) %>%
  left_join(am_alight_obs, by = "stn_code") %>%
  mutate(total_day = (am_tapin + replace_na(am_alight, 0)) / weekdays_may22)
p25_use <- quantile(existing_use$total_day, 0.25)

new_use <- new_pred %>%
  left_join(alight_exp, by = "stn_code") %>%
  mutate(board_day = per_day, alight_day = alight_pred / weekdays_may22,
         total_day = board_day + alight_day,
         role = case_when(alight_day > 1.5 * board_day ~ "Destination station",
                          board_day > 1.5 * alight_day ~ "Home station",
                          TRUE ~ "Mixed"),
         ghost_by_boarding = pred_exp < p25_existing,
         ghost_by_total_use = total_day < p25_use)

new_use %>%
  arrange(desc(total_day)) %>%
  transmute(stn_name = str_to_title(stn_name), line,
            boardings = fmt(board_day), alightings = fmt(alight_day), total = fmt(total_day),
            role, percentile_total = pct(ecdf(existing_use$total_day)(total_day), 0),
            ghost_by_boarding, ghost_by_total_use)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-roles
#| fig-cap: "New stations by predicted weekday morning boardings (Huff) and alightings (MCI). Points above the diagonal are destination stations; the dashed lines mark the lower quartile of existing stations on each axis."
#| fig-height: 6.5
p25_board <- p25_existing / weekdays_may22
p25_alight <- quantile(replace_na(existing_use$am_alight, 0) / weekdays_may22, 0.25)

ggplot(new_use, aes(board_day, alight_day, colour = role)) +
  geom_abline(linetype = 3, colour = "grey50") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = p25_board, linetype = 2, colour = "grey60") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = p25_alight, linetype = 2, colour = "grey60") +
  geom_point(aes(shape = line), size = 3.2) +
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(aes(label = str_to_title(stn_name)), size = 3.1, show.legend = FALSE,
                           max.overlaps = 30, seed = 626) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = label_comma()) + scale_y_log10(labels = label_comma()) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Destination station" = "#d95f02", "Home station" = "#176b87",
                                 "Mixed" = "#7570b3")) +
  labs(x = "Predicted AM-peak boardings per weekday (Huff, log)",
       y = "Predicted AM-peak alightings per weekday (MCI, log)", colour = NULL, shape = NULL) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
#| label: va-mci-reclass
#| include: false
rescued <- new_use %>% filter(ghost_by_boarding, !ghost_by_total_use) %>% arrange(desc(total_day)) %>% pull(stn_name)
still_low <- new_use %>% filter(ghost_by_total_use) %>% arrange(total_day) %>% pull(stn_name)
n_dest <- sum(new_use$role == "Destination station")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-new-station-map
#| fig-cap: "Interactive map: predicted morning use of the 29 new stations. Dot size is total predicted use (boardings + alightings; exact figures in the pop-up); colour is the station's role. Grey lines are the existing network."
new_use_sf <- new_stations %>%
  left_join(new_use %>% select(stn_code, board_day, alight_day, total_day, role), by = "stn_code") %>%
  mutate(across(c(board_day, alight_day, total_day), round), Station = str_to_title(stn_name))

as_leaflet(
  network_context() +
  tm_shape(net_new_sf) + tm_lines(col = "#d95f02", lwd = 3) +
  tm_shape(new_use_sf) +
  tm_dots(size = "total_day", fill = "role", fill_alpha = 0.9,
             size.scale = tm_scale_continuous(values.scale = 1.4),
             fill.scale = tm_scale_categorical(values = c("Destination station" = "#d95f02",
                                                          "Home station" = "#176b87",
                                                          "Mixed" = "#7570b3")),
             fill.legend = tm_legend(title = "Station role"),
             size.legend = tm_legend_hide(),
             id = "Station",
             popup.vars = c("Line" = "line", "Boardings / weekday" = "board_day",
                            "Alightings / weekday" = "alight_day", "Total / weekday" = "total_day",
                            "Role" = "role")))
```

**Insight.** Adding destination demand changes the ghost-station verdict.

- **`r n_dest` of the 29 new stations are destination stations**, where predicted alightings exceed boardings by more than half: `r str_c(str_to_title(new_use$stn_name[new_use$role == "Destination station"]), collapse = ", ")`. They serve the Jurong industrial estate and Jurong Innovation District, the Loyang, Defu and aviation employment areas, the NTU campus and the Tengah town centre.
- **`r length(rescued)` stations are "rescued" from ghost risk:** `r str_c(str_to_title(rescued), collapse = ", ")`. They fall below the lower quartile on boardings, but their combined morning use clears the lower quartile of existing stations. Judging them on boardings alone, as the Huff model must, would wrongly label them white elephants.
- **`r length(still_low)` stations remain below the lower quartile even with destination demand:** `r str_c(str_to_title(still_low), collapse = ", ")`. These are the genuine opening-day risks, and each has an explanation the planner should weigh:
  - Jurong Hill and Jurong Pier depend on industrial land that is still being redeveloped.
  - Nanyang Crescent and Peng Kang Hill serve the NTU campus, where students in campus halls are under-counted in the Census subzone population and the university is coded as one large educational parcel.
  - Aviation Park serves an airport-logistics cluster with shift-based demand outside the morning peak.

**Assumptions and limitations.**

- The MCI model inherits the *independence of irrelevant alternatives*: a new destination draws passengers from all other destinations in proportion to their current shares.
- Land-use floor area is a proxy for jobs, not an employment count.
- The 0.5-trip continuity correction slightly inflates the shares of very unattractive pairs.
- The chained Huff → MCI prediction carries the fixed-population assumption of the Huff scenario.

Even so, the MCI model adds substantive insight that the core analysis lacked. It separates stations that will be empty from stations that will be busy at the *other* end of the trip, and that distinction should drive any decision to defer or reprioritise station openings.

## Spatial autocorrelation of Huff residuals {#sec-va-moran}

**Question.** The Huff model assumes that, once distance and attraction are accounted for, the remaining errors are independent. If residuals cluster spatially, some spatial process is missing, for example town-level feeder-bus networks, and predictions in that area will be biased in a consistent direction.

**Method.** A k-nearest-neighbour weights matrix (k = 6, about the number of adjacent stations in Singapore's network) is built over station locations. Global Moran's I is tested by a 999-permutation Monte Carlo test, and local Moran's I (LISA) identifies where clusters occur (Chapters 9–10). The k-nearest-neighbour scheme is used because stations are points with very unequal spacing: a distance band would leave Tuas stations with no neighbours and give CBD stations dozens.

```{r}
#| label: va-moran
nb_knn <- knn2nb(knearneigh(st_coordinates(res_map), k = 6))
lw_knn <- nb2listw(nb_knn, style = "W")

moran_mc <- moran.mc(res_map$residual, lw_knn, nsim = 999)
moran_mc

# Robustness of the global test to the neighbour definition
map_dfr(c(4, 6, 8, 10), \(k) {
  lw <- nb2listw(knn2nb(knearneigh(st_coordinates(res_map), k = k)), style = "W")
  m <- moran.mc(res_map$residual, lw, nsim = 999)
  tibble(k = k, moran_I = round(m$statistic, 3), pseudo_p = m$p.value)
})

lisa <- localmoran(res_map$residual, lw_knn)
z_res <- as.numeric(scale(res_map$residual))
lag_res <- lag.listw(lw_knn, z_res)
res_map <- res_map %>%
  mutate(p_lisa = lisa[, 5],
         cluster = case_when(
           p_lisa >= 0.05 ~ "Not significant",
           z_res > 0 & lag_res > 0 ~ "High-High (under-predicted cluster)",
           z_res < 0 & lag_res < 0 ~ "Low-Low (over-predicted cluster)",
           z_res > 0 & lag_res < 0 ~ "High-Low",
           TRUE ~ "Low-High"))
count(st_drop_geometry(res_map), cluster)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-lisa
#| fig-cap: "Interactive map: LISA clusters of Huff model residuals (p < 0.05, k = 6 nearest neighbours). Click a station for its residual."
lisa_view <- res_map %>% mutate(Station = str_to_title(stn_name), Residual = round(residual))
as_leaflet(
  network_context() +
  tm_shape(lisa_view) +
  tm_dots(fill = "cluster", size = 0.6,
          fill.scale = tm_scale_categorical(values = c(
            "High-High (under-predicted cluster)" = "#2166ac",
            "Low-Low (over-predicted cluster)" = "#b2182b",
            "High-Low" = "#92c5de", "Low-High" = "#f4a582", "Not significant" = "grey70")),
          fill.legend = tm_legend(title = "LISA cluster"),
          id = "Station", popup.vars = c("Residual", "cluster")))
```

```{r}
#| label: lisa-numbers
#| include: false
lisa_tbl <- res_map %>% st_drop_geometry()
hh <- lisa_tbl %>% filter(str_starts(cluster, "High-High")) %>% pull(stn_name)
ll <- lisa_tbl %>% filter(str_starts(cluster, "Low-Low")) %>% pull(stn_name)
```

**Insight.** Global Moran's I is `r round(moran_mc$statistic, 3)` (pseudo p = `r signif(moran_mc$p.value, 2)`). It stays positive and significant for every neighbour definition from k = 4 to k = 10, so the Huff residuals are **regionally clustered, not independent**. The LISA map locates two main regimes:

- **Under-predicted (High-High) clusters**: the northern NSL corridor (`r str_c(str_to_title(intersect(hh, c("KRANJI", "MARSILING", "WOODLANDS", "YISHUN"))), collapse = ", ")`), consistent with cross-border commuters and long-distance feeder buses, and the Orchard–Novena–Stevens city-fringe belt (`r str_c(str_to_title(intersect(hh, c("NOVENA", "ORCHARD", "SOMERSET", "STEVENS"))), collapse = ", ")`), where schools, hotels and medical facilities generate non-residential morning boardings.
- **Over-predicted (Low-Low) cluster**: the east (`r str_c(str_to_title(intersect(ll, c("TAMPINES", "TAMPINES EAST", "TAMPINES WEST", "BEDOK", "BEDOK NORTH", "BEDOK RESERVOIR", "PASIR RIS", "TANAH MERAH", "EXPO", "UPPER CHANGI"))), collapse = ", ")`), where dense direct bus services to the Tampines regional centre and the Changi employment areas compete with rail.

**What this adds.** The core model's fit statistics say *how much* error there is; the spatial test shows the error is *regional*, which matters for forecasting. The CRL1 stations in the east (Pasir Ris East, Tampines North, Loyang and Aviation Park) sit inside the over-predicted cluster, so their forecasts in @fig-new-stations should be read as **upper bounds**. The JRL stations sit in the west, where no significant residual cluster is detected, so there is no evidence of a regional bias in their forecasts. A future model could absorb the eastern effect with a regional dummy or a bus-competition variable.

**Assumptions and limitations.** The k = 6 neighbour definition was chosen a priori; the robustness table shows the conclusion holds for k = 4 to 10. Moran's I on residuals tests for clustering but cannot identify its cause. With 164 points, local tests also carry a multiple-testing risk, so isolated significant stations should not be over-interpreted.

## Accessibility gains and equity (KD2SFCA) {#sec-va-access}

**Question.** Ridership is the operator's view. The sustainability view asks whether the new lines improve access for residents who are currently *least* served, or mainly add capacity where access is already good.

**Method.** The kernel-density two-step floating catchment area method (KD2SFCA, Chapter 17) is computed for every populated subzone before and after expansion. Supply is the station's service level (number of lines), demand is resident population, and the catchment is 2 km (walking plus a short feeder trip) with the default power of 2. Unlike the Hansen measure, 2SFCA accounts for competition for supply among residents and is bounded by the catchment, so adding a station far away cannot inflate everyone's score.

```{r}
#| label: va-access
acc <- function(D, supply) as.numeric(ac(p = origins_pt$pop, n = supply, D = D,
                                         d0 = 2, power = 2, family = "KD2SFCA"))
access <- origins_poly %>%
  mutate(acc_before = acc(D_base, dest_base$n_lines),
         acc_after = acc(D_exp, stations_exp$n_lines),
         gain = acc_after - acc_before) %>%
  filter(pop >= 100) %>%                      # ratios are unstable for near-empty subzones
  mutate(base_quintile = ntile(acc_before, 5))

access %>% st_drop_geometry() %>%
  group_by(base_quintile) %>%
  summarise(subzones = n(), residents = sum(pop),
            residents_gaining = sum(pop[gain > 1e-9]),
            share_residents_gaining = sum(pop[gain > 1e-9]) / sum(pop),
            median_gain_if_gaining = median(gain[gain > 1e-9]) * 1e5) %>%
  mutate(base_quintile = c("Q1 (least access)", "Q2", "Q3", "Q4", "Q5 (most access)"),
         residents = fmt(residents), residents_gaining = fmt(residents_gaining),
         share_residents_gaining = pct(share_residents_gaining),
         median_gain_if_gaining = round(median_gain_if_gaining, 2)) %>%
  rename(`median gain among gainers (x1e-5)` = median_gain_if_gaining)

cor.test(access$acc_before, access$gain, method = "spearman", exact = FALSE)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-access
#| fig-cap: "Change in KD2SFCA rail accessibility after JRL and CRL1 open (2 km catchment). Grey subzones are essentially unpopulated (fewer than 100 residents, or fewer than 100 per km²)."
#| fig-height: 6
tm_shape(subzones) + tm_polygons(fill = "grey90", col = "white", lwd = 0.2) +
  tm_shape(access %>% populated_for_map() %>% mutate(gain_e5 = gain * 1e5)) +
  tm_polygons(fill = "gain_e5",
              fill.scale = tm_scale_intervals(style = "fixed",
                                              breaks = c(0, 0.05, 0.5, 1, 2, Inf),
                                              labels = c("No change (< 0.05)", "0.05 to 0.5",
                                                         "0.5 to 1", "1 to 2", "> 2"),
                                              values = "brewer.yl_gn"),
              fill.legend = tm_legend(title = "Accessibility change (×10⁻⁵)"),
              col = "white", lwd = 0.2) +
  tm_shape(new_stations) + tm_dots(fill = "black", size = 0.12) +
  tm_title("Who gains rail access?") +
  tm_compass(position = c("right", "top"), size = 1.5) +
  tm_scalebar(position = c("left", "bottom")) +
  tm_layout(frame = FALSE, legend.outside = TRUE)
```

```{r}
#| label: access-numbers
#| include: false
share_gain_q <- function(q) with(access[access$base_quintile == q, ], sum(pop[gain > 1e-9]) / sum(pop))
q1_gain <- share_gain_q(1); q5_gain <- share_gain_q(5)
top_gain <- access %>% st_drop_geometry() %>% filter(pop >= 1000) %>% slice_max(gain, n = 5)
rho <- cor(access$acc_before, access$gain, method = "spearman")
n_loss <- sum(access$gain < -1e-9)
pop_gain <- sum(access$pop[access$gain > 1e-9])
```

**Insight.**

- **Gains go where access was weakest.** About `r pct(q1_gain, 0)` of residents in the lowest-access quintile gain accessibility, against `r pct(q5_gain, 0)` in the highest-access quintile. The Spearman correlation between baseline access and gain is `r round(rho, 2)`. The JRL and CRL1 therefore **narrow rather than widen** the existing access gap, a positive equity finding to set against the low *ridership* forecasts for some JRL stations.
- **The largest gains for populated subzones** are in `r str_c(str_to_title(top_gain$SUBZONE_N), collapse = ", ")`. These are the estates that the new lines bring within a short walk of rail for the first time.
- **No subzone loses access** (`r n_loss` subzones decline), but this is mechanical. KD2SFCA adds the new supply without reallocating existing stations' demand, so access cannot fall. The informative result is the *distribution* of the gains, shown above.

**Assumptions and limitations.** The supply measure (line count) ignores frequency and capacity. The 2 km catchment and power parameter are conventional, not calibrated. Straight-line distance understates access barriers such as expressways and rivers. The measure also uses Census 2020 population, so the Tengah gain is understated in the same way as Tengah ridership.

# Discussion and planning implications

**Addressing the objectives.**

- **O1.** A Huff model with two station attributes (lines served, LRT status) and an exponential access-distance decay ($\hat\lambda \approx$ `r round(lambda_hat, 2)` per km) explains about `r pct(r2_final, 0)` of the variation in morning boardings across 164 stations. It holds up out of sample (cross-validated R² `r round(mean(cv$test_R2), 2)`) and clearly beats the nearest-station (`r round(r2_r0, 2)`) and default-Huff (`r round(r2_r1, 2)`) benchmarks. The station-to-station SIM adds the complementary insight: *once on the network*, distance matters far less (elasticity `r round(b_dbc, 2)`). Residents are choosy about which station they walk to, not about how far they ride.
- **O2.** The strongest new stations are those inserted into mature HDB estates that currently lack a walkable MRT station, led by `r str_to_title(top3[1])`, `r str_to_title(top3[2])` and `r str_to_title(top3[3])`. CRL1 stations average almost twice the JRL's morning boardings. `r n_low` stations, all in employment areas, at NTU or in Tengah, fall below today's lower quartile on boardings. The MCI destination model shows that `r length(rescued)` of them (`r str_c(str_to_title(rescued), collapse = ", ")`) are busy enough as morning *destinations* to clear that bar, leaving `r length(still_low)` genuine opening-day risks.
- **O3.** Under fixed population the new lines redistribute, rather than create, morning boardings (about `r pct(share_div, 0)` moves to the new stations). Losses are concentrated in three clusters beside the new lines. Pioneer, Lakeside and Chinese Garden lose more than half their boardings, and four of the seven upgraded interchanges still lose tap-ins to new stations inside their catchments.

**Implications for sustainable rail planning.**

1. **Phase JRL openings to housing completions.** The Tengah sensitivity shows that the decisive variable is residents, not rails. A completion-linked threshold, using this model to estimate boardings at each stage of build-out, gives operators a transparent basis for deciding whether to open, partially open or defer a station, which is the decision faced at Hume and Buangkok.
2. **Re-plan feeder buses around the losing stations.** The stations losing 15% or more of morning boardings (the Jurong West EWL stations, the Bukit Panjang LRT, and the Kovan–Serangoon–Bishan belt) are where feeder routes should be re-drawn, so that bus kilometres follow the new market areas instead of duplicating rail.
3. **Plan interchange capacity, not just new stations.** Even where an upgraded interchange loses tap-ins, it gains transfers, which tap-in data do not record. Platform and corridor capacity at the seven interchanges is where crowding risk rises first.
4. **Appraise stations on both ends of the trip.** The chained Huff → MCI forecast shows that `r n_dest` of the 29 new stations are destination stations. Station-level appraisals should combine home-end and destination-end demand, plus the KD2SFCA access gains for the least-served residents. Any of these alone would mis-rank the stations.
5. **Read eastern forecasts as upper bounds.** The residual clustering shows the model systematically over-predicts in the east, so Pasir Ris East, Tampines North and Loyang may under-perform their forecasts.

# Limitations

- **Temporal mismatch.** OD flows are from May 2022 and population is from Census 2020; the scenario network is planned for 2028–2030. Population growth outside Tengah (for example, Tampines North and Bayshore) is not modelled.
- **Fixed total demand.** The trip rate $k$ is fixed, so the model cannot represent induced demand from better connectivity, and new-station boardings are entirely diverted from existing stations. True totals will be higher.
- **Attraction variables.** $A_j$ contains line count and LRT status only. Feeder-bus strength, cross-border demand, competing bus services, station amenities and service frequency are missing, as the significant residual clustering confirms. New stations are assumed to behave like an average single-line MRT station.
- **Distance.** Straight-line distance from subzone population-weighted centroids is used for station access. Walking-network or travel-time distances, for example from `sfnetworks` on an OSM path network, would be more realistic, especially across expressways and canals.
- **Morning peak only.** The Huff model explains home-end boardings and the MCI model explains morning destinations. Neither covers off-peak, evening or shift-work demand, which matters for stations such as Aviation Park.
- **Station coordinates.** New-station locations come from indicative Master Plan footprints and the station list from LTA announcements. Working names and exact locations may still change.

# Conclusion

A carefully cleaned dataset and a parsimonious, well-validated Huff model give planners a transparent way to forecast boardings at stations that do not yet exist. For the JRL and CRL1, the model gives a clear and actionable picture. Stations dropped into mature estates open into ready-made demand. Much of the JRL is a bet on future housing, and that bet can be managed by tying station openings to housing completions. The impacts on existing stations are local, predictable and largest along the western EWL. The new lines measurably improve access for the residents who are least served today.

# Saving results for the Executive Summary

The key outputs are saved so that the Executive Summary slides can be rebuilt from the same numbers without re-running the models.

```{r}
#| label: save-results
dir.create("data/rds", showWarnings = FALSE)
write_rds(list(
  subzones = st_simplify(subzones %>% select(SUBZONE_N), dTolerance = 15),
  stations = stations, new_stations = new_stations,
  net_base = net_base_sf, net_new = net_new_sf,
  calibrated = calibrated, new_pred = new_pred, tengah = tengah_cmp,
  impact_sf = impact_sf, market = market_change %>% select(SUBZONE_N, pop, change),
  access = access %>% select(SUBZONE_N, pop, gain, base_quintile),
  res_map = res_map %>% select(stn_code, residual, cluster),
  numbers = list(r2 = r2_final, r2_r0 = r2_r0, r2_r1 = r2_r1, cv_r2 = mean(cv$test_R2),
                 gamma = gamma_hat, delta = delta_hat, lambda = lambda_hat,
                 r2_power = decay_table$R2[1], b_dbc = b_dbc, r2_dbc = r2_dbc,
                 p25 = p25_existing, weekdays = weekdays_may22, share_div = share_div,
                 n_low = n_low, low_names = low_names, n_loss15 = n_loss15,
                 crl_mean = crl_mean, jrl_mean = jrl_mean, moran = moran_mc$statistic,
                 moran_p = moran_mc$p.value, q1_gain = q1_gain, q5_gain = q5_gain, rho = rho,
                 naive_new = length(naive_new), n_new_sz = n_new, pop_new_sz = pop_new,
                 mci_adj = adj_full, mci_null = adj_null, mci_alight_r2 = alight_r2,
                 n_dest = n_dest, rescued = rescued, still_low = still_low, b_mci = b_mci,
                 p25_use = p25_use),
  new_use = new_use),
  "data/rds/th3_results.rds", compress = "xz")
```
